title: 1979 AHSME Problem 29
statement: For each positive number \(x,\) let \[ f(x)= \frac{\begin{gathered} \left(x+\frac1x\right)^6\\ {}-\left(x^6+\frac1{x^6}\right)-2 \end{gathered}} {\begin{gathered} \left(x+\frac1x\right)^3\\ {}+\left(x^3+\frac1{x^3}\right) \end{gathered}}. \] The minimum value of \(f(x)\) is

solutions.text:
Let \(t=x+\frac{1}{x}\) and \(u=x^3+x^{-3}=t^3-3t.\) Since \(x^6+x^{-6}=u^2-2,\) the numerator is \[ \begin{aligned} t^6-u^2&=(t^3-u)(t^3+u)\\ &=3t(t^3+u). \end{aligned} \] The denominator is \(t^3+u,\) so \(f(x)=3t=3(x+\frac{1}{x}).\) For \(x\gt0,\) \(x+\frac{1}{x}\ge2,\) with equality at \(x=1.\) Thus the minimum is \(6.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Set \(t=x+\frac{1}{x}\) and write \(x^3+x^{-3}\) in terms of \(t\)
Factor the numerator as a difference of squares, then use \(x+\frac{1}{x}\ge2\)
